gap: None of the results ChatGPT got gives battery life with LDAC on. Soundcore's own figure for the Liberty 4 NC with LDAC and ANC on is 5 h per charge (25 h with the case). That is 5/8 = 62.5% of its 8 h ANC-only rating and about half of the 9 h 53 min SoundGuys measured, which is the figure ChatGPT used when it called it 'best ANC and battery'. Nothing rates the CMF Buds 2 Plus at 5.5 h in the same mode, and HiFi Oasis measured about 6 h with LDAC on the EarFun Air Pro 4+.
standout_why: I compared against SoundGuys' 'best wireless earbuds under $100' (cited in every chat) and Skimwire's 'best budget noise-cancelling earbuds 2026' (cited in 4 chats). SoundGuys gives ANC-on runtimes (Liberty 4 NC 9 h 53 min, Air Pro 4+ 6 h 17 min, Capsule3 Pro+ 3 h 53 min, CMF Buds 2 Plus 10 h 22 min with ANC off) and does not say which codec it tested with. Its only LDAC runtime is for the CMF Clip Pro, which isn't a candidate. Skimwire gives only rated hours and says nothing about LDAC's effect on battery. Neither page gives LDAC-mode hours for any candidate or says that LDAC cuts runtime by 25–50%. I could not open the SoundGuys LDAC roundup, the rtings1 page or our own page this run.
decides: For someone buying earbuds for LDAC, the claim 'Liberty 4 NC = best battery' falls apart. With LDAC and ANC on, its own rating (5 h) is below Nothing's rating for the CMF Buds 2 Plus (5.5 h) and below HiFi Oasis's measured 6 h for the EarFun Air Pro 4+. Note the 6 h is a reviewer's measurement and the other two are maker ratings, so they are not strictly the same basis. The Liberty 4 NC stays the pick for ANC, but its battery advantage only holds over AAC. Every candidate lands at roughly 5–6 h with LDAC and ANC on, so battery stops separating them in LDAC mode.
